pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded rows are all 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
test/done.test.js 'AC-2' marks item 2 done and checks both / and /?view=open list the two open items in id order.
test/done.test.js 'AC-3' marks 3 and 1 done and checks that /?view=done returns 200 with '✓ First item' then '✓ Third item'.
test/done.test.js 'AC-4' checks that all three items appear in id order with only the done one marked.
test/done.test.js 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for each view and for /, with the current view in <strong> and the others as links.
test/done.test.js 'AC-6' checks that Open, closed, empty and __proto__ values all return 400 with no <li>. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.
test/done.test.js 'AC-7' checks Nothing open., Nothing done yet., and No items yet. in all three views with an empty table. src/index.js does a COUNT fallback.

traffic/routes.json lists '/?view=done' and '/?view=all', but no test names AC-8 or reads routes.json for these routes. The spec does not mark the item 'verified by review'. test/traffic.test.js only gained query support in its fake app. The PR body says test/done.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8, which is not true for AC-8.

findings.what: No test proves AC-8. Nothing asserts that traffic/routes.json contains /?view=done and /?view=all, or that the traffic round requests them. Dropping the routes would break no test.
findings.fix: Add a test titled with AC-8 that imports ROUTES from traffic/src/index.js and expects it to contain '/?view=done' and '/?view=all'. Better, run a scheduled round against the fake app and check that those paths were seen.

findings.what: The PR body says test/done.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8. The file has no AC-8 test.
findings.fix: Add the AC-8 test, or correct the claim.

lenses.note: The change works from specs/done-items.md. The decisions are followed: the list opens on open items, and the view is a query parameter with no cookie.

AC-1 to AC-7 are met with named tests. AC-8 has no naming test. All six state-table rows have tests. No commit edits the spec after the go: the spec is added once, and the follow-up commit only deletes 4 blank test lines.
The done.test.js assertions check behaviour. The npm tests were not run here; CI runs them. The AC-8 gap is reported as a finding.
README describes the new views. The spec is included.

The view is whitelisted with Object.hasOwn and the SQL fragments are constants, so there is no injection. The empty-table check is correct. The traffic-config regex now allows a query string and still refuses spaces and #.
No injection or secrets. User input only selects a key from a fixed map, and titles stay HTML-escaped.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or UI files. The nav behaviour is covered under AC-5.
The diff touches no UI framework or browser flow files. The PR states there are no screenshots.
The title is under 72 characters. The claim that done.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8 is false for AC-8.
